plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, fragrant, ruffled blooms unfold like silk pom-poms on glossy green foliage. Whole gardens turn into clouds of blush, rose and cream.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring, typically May to early June in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, including the United States, Europe and China, where the plant is native
plants.funFact: Peonies have been cultivated in China for more than 1,000 years, and a single plant can live and bloom for decades.

plants.name: Iris germanica
plants.description: Tall, sword-leaved stems carry ruffled flowers with three upright petals and three drooping falls. Each fall wears a fuzzy 'beard' that guides pollinators inward.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer, commonly May in temperate Northern Hemisphere regions
plants.location: Gardens across North America and Europe, with origins in the Mediterranean region
plants.funFact: The iris is named for the Greek goddess of the rainbow, and the genus includes flowers in nearly every color of the spectrum.

plants.name: Rosa canina
plants.description: A tangled, arching wild shrub throws out delicate five-petaled flowers with golden centers along hedgerows and woodland edges. It later bears bright red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May through June and into early summer in Europe
plants.location: Hedgerows, scrub and woodland margins across Europe, western Asia and northwest Africa
plants.funFact: Rose hips from this species are very rich in vitamin C, and were gathered in Britain during World War II to make syrup.
